states.edition: Wisconsin Uniform Dwelling Code, SPS 320–325 (Wisconsin's own code, not the IRC)
states.differs_from_app: Row is right that the UDC is Wisconsin's own code. Fill in since = 1980 (UDC took effect June 1, 1980; chapters current through Register Nov 2024). The guard trigger is 24 in., not 30 in. (SPS 321.04(3)(c)); footings must be at least 48 in. below adjacent grade statewide (SPS 321.16) — make sure the app doesn't use a county frost table here.
notes: Guards are required on decks, porches and landings more than 24 in. above grade; outdoors, measure from the lowest point within 3 ft of the edge; guards must be at least 36 in. high and stop a 4 3/8 in. sphere (SPS 321.04(3)(c)).
Risers 8 in. max, treads 9 in. min (SPS 321.04(2)).
Footings go below frost penetration or at least 48 in. below adjacent grade, whichever is deeper (SPS 321.16).

Attached decks, and detached decks that serve an exit, must meet the UDC; decks built to SPS 325 Appendix B/C are deemed to comply (SPS 321.225). Detached decks not serving an exit are exempt from the UDC (SPS 320.05(5)).
Deck live load is 40 psf (Table 321.02-1); wind is 20 psf or per ASCE 7-05, and roof snow loads come from the UDC zone map, so there is no IRC-style wind mph or ground-snow value.

states.edition: Iowa State Building Code, 481 IAC ch. 301 — residential: 2024 IRC with Iowa amendments (481—301.8)
states.differs_from_app: Basis is now the 2024 IRC, not 2021: 481—301.8 adopts the 2024 IRC (ARC 9474C, effective Sept 10, 2025), so since = 2025. The rules also moved from 661 IAC (Public Safety) to 481 IAC (Inspections, Appeals & Licensing) on 11/26/2025. The 'binds only where adopted' note stands: it applies to state-funded work and where a city or county adopts it by ordinance (Iowa Code 103A.12). Big cities adopt the IRC directly: Des Moines and Cedar Rapids are on the 2024 IRC, Davenport on the 2021 IRC.
notes: Table R301.2 values are set by the project's location (481—301.8(3)); there is no statewide table.
Iowa's residential amendments don't touch stairs or guards, so the IRC's 7 3/4 in. riser, 10 in. tread and 36 in. guard apply (confirmed in the Cedar Rapids deck handout).

counties.edition: 2015 Michigan Residential Code (2015 IRC with Part 5 amendments), effective Feb 8, 2016; 2021 MRC stayed by court order

Plans must show footing sizes, post sizes, joist and beam spans with lumber species and grade, attachment, stair, guard and handrail details. Replacing deck boards also needs a permit.

Decks more than 24 in. above grade need post-to-beam angle bracing. Guards are required more than 30 in. above grade and must carry a 200 lb load. Risers 8 1/4 in. max, treads 9 in. min.
Inspections: open post hole, structural frame, final.
counties.note: Troy's deck guide (rev. 11/12/25) does not state a footing depth; the 42 in. is the statewide MRC rule. Troy notes the 2021 MRC is paused and the 2015 code governs.

Footings at least 48 in. deep. Guards at least 36 in. high on any deck more than 2 ft above ground. Stairs with more than 3 risers need a handrail, with guard openings that stop a 4 3/8 in. ball.
Decks under 3 ft high can usually extend to the lot line; decks 3 ft or higher must meet the district setbacks.

For decks over 3 ft high, submit a site plan to scale (e.g. 1 in. = 20 ft). Construction drawings at a common scale (e.g. 1/4 in. = 1 ft) show deck size, posts, beams and joists. Lakefront lots need a surveyor's survey.

counties.jurisdiction: City of Waukesha Community Development – Building Inspection (county seat and largest city), enforcing the Wisconsin UDC
counties.edition: Wisconsin Uniform Dwelling Code, SPS 320–325 (statewide; not IRC-based)
counties.wind_basis: UDC uses 20 psf horizontal/uplift or ASCE 7-05 loads, not an IRC wind speed
deck_notes: New decks need a building permit with a current, accurate plat of survey showing property lines, existing buildings and the deck's size and location.
Plans show post size and spacing, footing diameter and depth, joist and beam sizes, spacing and spans, the ledger/post attachment, decking, stairs, guards, and any doors onto the deck.

Decks 12 in. or more above grade that are attached to, or within 10 ft of, the house must meet side-yard setbacks and may project up to 10 ft into the rear yard. Freestanding decks must be at least 10 ft from the house and 3 ft from lot lines.
A deck reached from inside the house needs an electrical outlet within its perimeter, on a separate electrical permit.
Inspections: footings/post holes before concrete, framing, final.
counties.note: Waukesha's page sets no footing depth of its own; the 48 in. is the statewide UDC minimum.

counties.jurisdiction: State of Minnesota (Minn. R. 1303/1309 statewide criteria); deck rules from City of Minneapolis Construction Code Services
counties.edition: 2020 Minnesota Residential Code (Minn. R. ch. 1309, 2018 IRC basis), effective March 31, 2020
counties.wind_basis: 2018 IRC Figure R301.2(5)A (ultimate design wind speed); statewide MN Table R301.2(1)
deck_notes: Minneapolis requires a permit when the deck is more than 30 in. above grade, attached to the house, or part of an accessible route.
Submit a scaled, dimensioned site plan showing the deck's size and distances to property lines and nearby structures. Property lines must be located by a surveyor or by found markers.

Plans and a section drawing must show footing type, depth and width (at least 14 in. round or 12 in. square), the ledger (2x8 min., no smaller than the joists), lateral-load connections, beams, guards and stairs.
Guards at least 36 in. high where more than 30 in. above grade, with 4 in. sphere openings. A graspable handrail is required at 4 or more risers, and a bottom landing at every stair.
counties.note: Hennepin is Frost Zone II (42 in.) and 50 psf ground snow by Minn. R. 1303.1600/1700. Termite is left to the jurisdiction in MN's table and not published. Minneapolis deck guide updated 06/2025.

counties.jurisdiction: City of Des Moines Permit & Development Center (county seat and largest city) — published design criteria
counties.edition: 2024 IRC with Des Moines amendments, effective Jan 1, 2026
counties.wind_basis: Des Moines design criteria (topographic effects none; no special wind region)
deck_notes: Apply online through the Customer Self Service portal ('Residential Other Building Permit'). Include a site plan with approximate distances to property lines and a deck plan showing the deck's height above grade.

Frost depth is 42 in. Footings are at least 12 in. thick, and round footing diameter goes from 8 in. at 10 sq ft to 20 in. at 80 sq ft of tributary area (40 psf live, 2,000 psf soil). Freestanding non-frost-protected decks also use this table.
Ledgers 2x8 minimum. No attaching to house cantilevers or brick veneer without specialty fasteners or engineering, and a hot tub requires structural engineering.
Guards at least 36 in. high (34 in. on stairs), posts no more than 6 ft apart and never notched, 4 in. sphere rule. Inspections: footings, framing, final.
counties.note: The deck handout is written to the 2021 IRC; the city moved to the 2024 IRC on Jan 1, 2026. The criteria also list decay slight to moderate, winter design 0°F, air freezing index 1833.

counties.jurisdiction: City of Cedar Rapids Building Services (county seat and largest city)
counties.edition: 2024 IRC with local amendments (City of Cedar Rapids)
deck_notes: Fill in the city's deck building guide and add a site plan showing project dimensions, nearby buildings, utilities, property lines and easements, post locations and spacing, and joist/beam spans.
Footings at least 42 in. deep, sized with the handout's footing table, and inspected before the pour.
Ledgers 2x8 minimum and may not carry beam or girder loads. Guards at least 36 in. high where more than 30 in. above grade. Risers 7 3/4 in. max, treads 10 in. min, stairs at least 36 in. wide.
counties.note: The deck handout file is labeled 2021 IRC while the city's codes page lists the 2024 IRC. The city publishes no snow, wind or seismic values.

counties.jurisdiction: Scott County Planning & Development (unincorporated Scott County); the City of Davenport (county seat, largest city) runs its own department
counties.edition: Davenport: 2021 IRC with local amendments (City Code ch. 15.12). Unincorporated Scott County: County Code ch. 5 'Construction Codes' (edition not confirmed).
deck_notes: Scott County requires a building permit for every deck. Submit a plot plan with dimensions to the property lines and a plan with the deck size, lumber sizes, and post and beam locations.
Footings for unroofed decks are 12 in. diameter x 42 in. deep and inspected before the pour; roofed decks have different standards.
Decks more than 30 in. above grade need a guard with the top rail at least 36 in. above the deck and spindles no more than 4 in. apart.
Davenport exempts platforms/decks that serve no door, are no more than 30 in. above grade, aren't attached to a structure, and aren't over a basement or story below.
counties.note: The 42 in. comes from the county deck page. Davenport's IRC amendments (City Code 15.12) couldn't be read (Municode 403), so Davenport climatic values are unknown.
